hints: Focus on the shape around each carbon, as double bonds give flat trigonal planar centres while single bonds give tetrahedral 3D centres.
Look at 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene, $(	ext{CH}_3)_2	ext{C}=	ext{C}(	ext{CH}_3)_2$, where the two $	ext{C}=	ext{C}$ carbons and the four methyl carbons attached to them are all held in one flat plane.
Remember that any three atoms always define a plane, but six atoms in a puckered ring cannot, so compare propane with cyclohexane to finish the list.
walkthrough:
**Recall what makes carbons planar**

Think shape first. A $\text{C}=\text{C}$ carbon is $sp^2$ and trigonal planar, so it and the three atoms joined to it lie flat in one plane. A saturated $sp^3$ carbon is tetrahedral, so its four bonds point out in 3D.

Rule: $\text{C}=\text{C}$ centre = flat, $\text{C}-\text{C}$ centre = 3D

**Check molecule 1: 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene**

The structure is $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)_2$. Both central carbons are $sp^2$.

Each $\text{C}=\text{C}$ carbon has two methyl groups attached in its trigonal plane, so all six carbons lie in the same plane. So 1 is correct.
$$ (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{C}=\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)_2 \text{ : all 6 C planar} $$

**Check molecule 2: propane**

Propane is $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_3$ with only three carbons.

Any three points in space always define a plane, even though each carbon is tetrahedral $sp^3$. So all three carbons must be coplanar. So 2 is correct.

**Check molecule 3: cyclohexane**

Cyclohexane is $\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}$, all $sp^3$ single bonds. It puckers into a chair conformation to reduce strain.

The six carbons are not flat, they point up and down out of the plane. So 3 is incorrect.

Conclusion: 1 and 2 only are correct.

options.A: Incorrect because it includes all three molecules. Cyclohexane is not planar as it adopts a puckered chair shape with $sp^3$ carbons, so 3 fails.
options.B: Correct because 1 and 2 only are planar. In 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene the $\text{C}=\text{C}$ unit holds all six carbons in one trigonal planar system, and in propane three carbons always define a single plane.
options.C: Incorrect because it pairs 2 with 3 but leaves out 1. Molecule 1 is planar and should be included, while molecule 3 cyclohexane is puckered and should not be included.
options.D: Incorrect because it includes only 1. Molecule 1 is indeed planar, but molecule 2 propane is also planar since any three carbon atoms lie in the same plane, so 2 is wrongly omitted.
